extracted.intended_audience: comedy fans, stand-up comedians, festival programmers, and industry professionals (agents/bookers/critics)
extracted.subtask_description: A critical review of a comedy festival showcase (Just For Laughs New Faces), assessing booking choices, performer suitability, material, and the festival's policies and ethics. Focus is on how programmers select and present emerging comedians and what that means for careers.

rubrics_metrics.name: New Faces should be truly 'new' (novelty/freshness)
rubrics_metrics.description: New Faces used to be the be-all, end-all credit for stand-up comedians coming up in the business ... By the time I started attending Montreal’s JFL ... some of the New Faces were no longer even New Faces to anyone in the industry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion: a New Faces slot should go to performers who are genuinely emerging and relatively undiscovered by industry decision-makers. Anti-pattern: booking performers who already have managers/agents, television credits, or half-hour specials undermines the showcase's purpose. Examples from the page: performers who had recent TV spots or taped half-hours questioned as to 'how is he a New Face, exactly?'

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior credits and exposure should determine eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: If you’ve got a cushy gig in comedy already, what is New Faces supposed to do for you ... He taped a half-hour special for Comedy Central a few days after this showcase!
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion: evaluate candidates by existing TV appearances, development deals, half-hour/Netflix specials, late-night debuts, staff-writing credits, festival history, and prior industry showcases. Guidance: those with significant credits are less appropriate for a 'New Faces' slot. Use explicit credit checks as a screening metric.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose/value — New Faces should function as a discovery/career pipeline
rubrics_metrics.description: Over the course of a hot week, a stand-up could go from no-name to New Face to six-figure development deal ... If you’ve got a cushy gig in comedy already, what is New Faces supposed to do for you, when it could be doing something for a comedian who desperately needs a break?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion: bookers should prioritize performers who will materially benefit from discovery (development deals, network attention) rather than those already established. Scoring note: prioritize potential for upward career mobility and demonstrable lack of prior industry access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate showcase placement (characters vs stand‑up vs creators)
rubrics_metrics.description: JFL also added a Characters showcase ... Sarah Sherman aka Sarah Squirm ... maybe should’ve been in the Characters showcase instead? Or did JFL not know what to do with her?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion: match performer type (character act, visual performance, creator/online talent, traditional stand-up) to the correct showcase. Anti-pattern: placing a character or visual act in a straight stand-up slot where their act is out of context. Guidance: assess format and medium of the material when assigning showcases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinct voice and storytelling potential
rubrics_metrics.description: This guy has a story to tell, development-wise, and has a distinct voice ... She has a great sense of humor about not only being trans, but also about what that means in today’s society.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion: look for performers with a clear, individual point-of-view and storytelling instincts that lend themselves to longer sets or writers' rooms. Guidance: identify whether the performer has 'a story to tell' and room to develop into half-hours/hours or staff-writing roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Material freshness, topicality, and relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: His jokes were very current, dealing with lessons he’s learned from the pandemic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion: evaluate whether jokes engage contemporary topics in a way that feels current and resonant. Scoring note: topical material that demonstrates awareness of recent events (e.g., pandemic, social movements) scores higher for immediacy; beware of material that dates quickly or relies solely on passing trends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depth appropriate to set length (development across 15/30/60 minutes)
rubrics_metrics.description: All of McBride’s material was focused on playing on audience’s misconceptions about trans people, which OK for a start. 'But hopefully a 15-minute set or half-hour or an hour has other places to go.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion: assess whether a performer’s material shows sufficient range for the advertised set length (e.g., a 15-minute set should show more than one gag/angle; a half-hour needs sustained throughlines). Anti-pattern: relying on a single theme or gimmick for longer formats without development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selective content warnings and consistent moderation
rubrics_metrics.description: Why did the festival reissue this warning not once, but twice ... JFL felt compelled only during Tom’s bit about exploring a non-monogamous relationship to plaster a warning onscreen above the comedian.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion: festival content-warnings should be applied consistently and transparently. Anti-pattern: singling out one performer (especially a marginalized performer) with warnings that are not used for others with similar material; this can appear discriminatory. Guidance: create objective standards for when to display content/advisory notices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Festival ethics, accountability, and institutional trust
rubrics_metrics.description: Singer resigned shortly before this year’s festival, but not before booking it once more. He admitted to making offensive comments ... JFL’s founder, Gilbert Rozon, had himself stepped down in 2017 only after his own history of sexual harassment and assault came to light anew.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion: evaluate the festival's credibility based on how it handles harassment/scandal and whether it holds staff/bookers accountable. Scoring note: festivals that ignore or mishandle serious allegations lose legitimacy and harm performers, particularly marginalized groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Booking fairness vs commercial partnerships and redundancy
rubrics_metrics.description: JFL already has a cozy deal with Variety magazine to showcase the 10 Comics To Watch each July ... Some of these New Faces are better suited for that showcase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion: consider whether bookings duplicate other festival showcases or commercial partnerships, reducing overall opportunities. Anti-pattern: using New Faces slots to re-promote the same artists across multiple festival-promoted lists rather than expanding the pool of working comics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Livestream mechanics affect industry behavior and privacy
rubrics_metrics.description: The livestreams included both a public chat feature next to the screen, as well as an attendee list that allowed anyone with a pass to private message anyone else. Funnunnnnnnnnn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion: when producing livestreamed showcases, evaluate how platform features (chat, attendee lists, private messaging) change the dynamics of discovery, privacy, and networking. Guidance: festivals should anticipate and manage how these tools can be used by industry to judge or contact performers, and mitigate harassment/privacy risks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identity‑based material requires careful navigation
rubrics_metrics.description: Tom joked about using they/them pronouns to sound less lonely ... even attempting a men and women are different joke from a nonbinary perspective was fraught with danger. 'Just assume everything I’m about to say is wrong!'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion: assess whether material that engages identity (gender, transness, race, religion) does so with nuance and self-awareness rather than punching down or relying on stereotypes. Scoring note: identity-driven jokes that clearly interrogate assumptions or subvert stereotypes score higher; material that plays into harm or single-outting can require festival advisories or sensitive placement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signal of career-readiness: writing and production credits
rubrics_metrics.description: Tom’s credits include staff writing for Taika Waititi’s HBO Max series ... Wally Baram ... has written for FX/Hulu’s What We Do In The Shadows, HBO’s Betty ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion: use writing/production credits as indicators of a performer’s trajectory toward writers' rooms, TV development, or multi‑platform work. Guidance: while these credits may make a performer less 'new', they also signal suitability for industry roles and might inform a festival's choice to promote them through other programming (writers showcases, panels).
